item.title: SpaceX Crew-13 reaches ISS in record eight-hour flight with first Black woman commander
item.description:
Four astronauts arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday after completing the fastest crewed flight by a U.S. spacecraft, docking just about eight hours after launching from Florida. The historic mission, designated Crew-13, was launched by SpaceX for NASA and marked two significant milestones: it set a new U.S. speed record for transit to the orbiting laboratory, and it featured the first Black woman to command a crew into orbit.
Commander Jessica Watkins, a geologist who previously worked on NASA's Curiosity Mars rover and flew to space in 2022, led the crew alongside NASA pilot Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov. The launch from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station occurred after a three-week delay to repair a leaking fuel system on the Dragon capsule, named Grace. Despite threatening weather conditions, the skies cleared in time for a safe liftoff.

item.title: Eritrea cuts diplomatic ties with Ethiopia after embassy closure order
item.description:
Eritrea has severed diplomatic relations with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa ordered the closure of Ethiopia’s embassy in Asmara and declared 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata, according to Reuters. The decision marks a sharp deterioration in relations between the neighboring countries, which have a long history of conflict and political tension.
The diplomatic rupture came after explosions were reportedly heard overnight in Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa, according to diplomatic sources cited in the report. The available information does not establish whether the explosions were connected to the diplomatic dispute or identify their cause. Authorities had not publicly provided a detailed explanation of the blasts at the time of the report.

item.title: Wynonna Judd Confronts Family Secrets and Grief on New Album 'The Hard Truth'
item.description: Country music legend Wynonna Judd is releasing her first album in a decade, titled 'The Hard Truth,' marking a deeply personal turning point in her career. For the first time, she serves as the primary songwriter on a record, co-writing most of the songs with her husband, Cactus Moser. The album emerges from a grueling yet clarifying creative process that forced Judd to confront long-guarded family secrets and unresolved grief following the 2022 suicide of her mother and former musical partner, Naomi Judd. In interviews with The New York Times and other outlets, Judd describes walking to the studio each day on her Tennessee farm and crying the entire way home, underscoring the emotional toll of the project. The songs address her complicated relationship with Naomi, including anger and partial forgiveness over the revelation that her biological father—whom she never met—was kept secret for three decades. item.description: The Moss & Fog website has undergone a significant redesign, introducing a refreshed homepage and new navigation features. The redesign focuses on five distinct worlds: Nature, Architecture, Design, Travel, and Science, each now featuring full-width covers with large titles over compelling stories. Within each world, users can narrow their focus using small buttons (e.g., Animals or Underwater in Nature, Furniture or Skyscrapers in Architecture) without leaving the page. The homepage also includes a ranked list of popular stories and a color explorer tool within each world. The redesign enhances sharing capabilities, with small share buttons on every story card that offer options for sharing via social media platforms, email, or copying a link. The Moss & Fog Shop has also been updated with a special Halloween-themed promotion called 'The Witching Hours,' offering 25% off on eleven October-themed items from Friday midnight to Saturday midnight Pacific Time. item.title: Seth Meyers Debunks Trump's Claim of 107 Million Convention Views
item.description: Late Night host Seth Meyers addressed President Donald Trump's recent claim about the Republican National Convention's viewership on his Thursday show. Trump had stated during a press conference that the convention garnered 107 million views, surpassing the NFL's 25 million viewers for its season opener. Meyers fact-checked the claim, noting that while Trump's figure was technically accurate when aggregating across all platforms including delayed viewing statistics, the actual live audience was significantly lower. According to Meyers, the convention's television and streaming audience was approximately 3.3 million viewers, compared to the NFL's 25.1 million for its season opener. Meyers sarcastically remarked that Trump's doctors must be putting him through the concussion protocol, drawing a parallel between Trump's health concerns and the implausibility of his claim. item.title: HBO's Legal Drama 'War' Premieres with Divorce Battle and Corporate Espionage
item.description: HBO's new legal drama 'War' has made a strong debut with its Season 1 premiere, establishing itself as a compelling and addictive series that promises to be a major water-cooler show. The premiere introduces two rival London law firms, Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne, and their high-stakes clients: social media mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) and his movie star wife Carla Duval (Sienna Miller). Their marriage, now loveless, is heading toward a public and expensive divorce. Carla seeks to leave the marriage and take Morgan's fortune, but their prenuptial agreement is designed to protect Morgan unless he has fulfilled his obligations, which he has not. Morgan's infidelity, documented through a 'honey trap' orchestrated by Carla's younger actress friend, becomes the catalyst for the legal battle. The premiere features a dramatic moment where Carla is served divorce papers on the red carpet at her movie premiere, a move reminiscent of a real-life incident involving Olivia Wilde.

The movie follows Vijay's continued efforts to protect his family after the events of Drishyam 2, with a new storyline that diverges from the Malayalam Drishyam 3. Early reviews from trade analyst Taran Adarsh have praised the film as 'OUTSTANDING' with a 4.5-star rating, calling it the 'BEST FILM' in the franchise and a 'SURE-SHOT BLOCKBUSTER.' Adarsh highlighted the film's strong direction and writing, noting that director Abhishek Pathak successfully took the story forward without recycling the formula of earlier films. item.description: Drishyam 3: The Conclusion, the final installment in the Hindi Drishyam franchise, is set to release in theaters on October 2, 2026, with high expectations for a record-breaking box office opening. Trade estimates predict the film will achieve a net opening of over ₹50 crore, making it the highest opening for a Hindi film this year. The advance booking figures show strong performance, with ₹44.33 crore sold across six show dates, including ₹23.69 crore on the opening day (Friday, October 2). Maharashtra leads as the top state with ₹7.46 crore, followed by Delhi at ₹5.23 crore and Gujarat at ₹1.68 crore. item.title: Trump Begins Midterm Campaign With Rally in Oklahoma, Far From Competitive Districts
item.description: President Donald Trump recently held his first rally in Oklahoma since his controversial and sparsely attended COVID-era event, marking the start of his midterm campaign tour. The rally, held in Durant, Oklahoma, took place in a region that strongly supported Trump in the 2024 election, with the closest competitive House district located 350 miles away. Trump claimed he would visit all 35 swing House seats to help Republicans, but the nearest toss-up seat is 350 miles away from the rally site in Durant. During his speech, Trump expressed gratitude to Oklahoma voters for their 'unbelievable' support, noting he won all 77 counties in the state. He also repeated several false claims, including that he had brought in $21 trillion in foreign investment, that new factories were being built due to his tariffs, and that inflation had been reduced. item.description: Republican senators are expressing strong disapproval of President Donald Trump's government-funded advertisements that promote his image and political agenda. According to a report by The Bulwark, multiple GOP senators have voiced concerns about the ads, which feature Trump's voice promising supporters a 'reckoning' with his enemies. The advertisements, airing during NFL games, depict Trump vowing to 'demolish the deep state' and 'rout the fake news media' as he walks down a hallway. Cornyn explicitly stated that the president is not permitted to run such government-funded ads, answering 'no' when asked if Trump is allowed to do so. item.title: Shadow Lion Announces Documentary on Dubai Basketball's Championship Journey
item.description: Shadow Lion, the company founded by NFL legend Tom Brady, is developing a documentary titled 'Yalla, Dubai: From Startup to Championship' that chronicles the rise of Dubai Basketball to ABA League champions. The film follows the team from its 2023 launch to winning the ABA League title in their second full season, defeating Partizan 3-1 in the finals in June. item.description: According to former federal prosecutor Joyce Vance, President Donald Trump's legal challenges are accumulating rapidly, outpacing the Supreme Court's ability to provide relief. Vance, who previously served as U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Alabama, outlined several recent court decisions across four cities that have negatively impacted the Trump administration. The judge noted the government had already determined no crime occurred. item.title: Trump's Dairy Trade War with Canada Leaves Farmers in Crisis
item.description: President Donald Trump's trade policies targeting Canada have had unintended consequences for U.S. dairy producers, contradicting his claims of protecting American agriculture. According to a recent article in The Bulwark by economics editor Catherine Rampell, U.S. dairy farmers, whom Trump has repeatedly positioned as beneficiaries of his trade war, are now expressing frustration and calling for an end to the tariffs. Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian dairy ranging from 250% to 400%, but these rates only apply to sales exceeding a tariff-free quota established under the USMCA trade agreement. Rampell notes that U.S. dairy producers have never approached this quota, and the U.S. actually exports three times more dairy to Canada than it imports. item.description: The New York Times reported that Republican senators are criticizing their own party's handling of the final days of Congress, with many expressing frustration over wasted floor time on votes that were destined to fail. The senators argued that the party spent valuable time staging symbolic votes on issues like rising costs, which produced no meaningful results. Senator Jim Justice (R-WV) warned that if voters cannot afford basic necessities, they will have a 'real problem with us,' emphasizing the need for the party to address ordinary Americans' financial struggles. The article notes that Republicans face a challenging political climate, with voters concerned about the economy, inflation, and the ongoing conflict in Iran, while President Donald Trump's approval ratings remain low. item.title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Brain Health Risks When Combined with Severe Caloric Restriction, Expert Warns
item.description: Popular weight-loss medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which belong to the GLP-1 drug class, may pose risks to brain health when combined with severe caloric restriction, according to Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington. Dr. Wood explained that the brain is the body's most energy-hungry organ and requires a steady supply of nutrients to maintain its structure and function. During rapid weight loss or extreme dieting, the brain may be deprived of essential energy and nutrients, potentially leading to the shrinkage of brain tissue. This phenomenon was illustrated by a study on marathon runners, where the brain's white matter temporarily shrank due to insufficient energy during the race, but recovered after refueling. item.title: Former Trump Aide Cites Internal Fractures and Staff Exodus as MAGA Coalition Weakens
item.description: A former Trump administration official has stated that fractures within the president's coalition are causing a significant number of senior staff to leave the White House, with some describing the situation as 'armageddon.' According to a report by the Daily Mail, which interviewed roughly six current and former administration aides, the departures include high-ranking officials such as Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, White House counsel David Warrington, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, and deputy chief of staff James Blair. These departures have been attributed to disagreements over the administration's direction, particularly regarding the Iran war and rising prices. Wolff, who has written four books about Trump, discussed this during a new episode of 'Inside Trump's Head,' a podcast he co-hosts with Joanna Coles of The Daily Beast. He explained that Trump's rage is often directed at female aides, citing a moment when cameras captured Trump berating his aide Natalie Harp while she maintained a smile, seemingly taking the abuse. He described Trump as a man with 'no restraints,' who expresses his thoughts bluntly without filtering, stating, 'If he feels it, if he thinks it, he expresses it, and his powers of expression are... blunt force.' item.description: The article presents a collection of vintage photographs capturing British actress Joan Collins during the filming of the 1957 drama 'Island in the Sun' in Barbados. These images showcase Collins at a pivotal moment in her career, as she was rising to international prominence. The photos highlight her striking features, elegant style, and natural screen presence both during filming and in quieter moments between takes. The article notes that the film provided Collins with a prominent role against the lush Caribbean backdrop of Barbados, offering a glamorous glimpse into her early Hollywood career. item.description: Texas Governor Greg Abbott (R) has been linked to Elon Musk through what legal analyst Katie Phang describes as a 'backscratching' relationship, involving state grants and tax breaks for Musk's companies. In a recent video interview with Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa, Phang highlighted that Starlink received $110 million upfront from the Texas Broadband Office, while SpaceX secured a tax break shortly after Musk donated $500,000 to Abbott's reelection campaign. Phang argued that this arrangement exemplifies a 'power trifecta' in Texas, where the Republican Party controls the state house, state senate, and governor's office. She emphasized that with one-party rule, there is 'no daylight between Greg Abbott and the billionaires,' and criticized the lack of accountability for the state's 'woefully, sadly miserable' conditions. Psaki highlighted Trump's recent interview with Time Magazine, where he seemed confused and disinterested in his presidential duties, particularly regarding the upcoming midterm elections. item.title: Conservation Groups Challenge Trump Administration's Rule Change on Endangered Species Act
item.description: Conservation groups have updated their legal challenge against the Trump administration's recent rule change that redefines 'harm' under the Endangered Species Act (ESA). The coalition, including organizations such as the Center for Biological Diversity, Columbia Riverkeeper, and Earthjustice, argues that the new interpretation, which allows for 'incidental' killing of protected species, violates the ESA's plain language and purpose. The rule change, effective September 14, 2026, was implemented through memos from US Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik and NOAA General Counsel John Luce. These memos direct agencies to interpret the ESA as only prohibiting intentional killing or wounding of endangered species, effectively permitting incidental harm. item.title: Federal Judge Rules Trump Administration Violated Constitution by Firing Court-Appointed U.S. Attorney
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that the Trump administration violated constitutional limits on presidential power by abruptly firing a court-appointed U.S. attorney in Seattle. Judge Stanley Bastian, an Obama appointee, ordered the reinstatement of Roger Rogoff, a veteran prosecutor selected by Western District of Washington judges to lead the Seattle U.S. attorney's office. The firing occurred within an hour of Rogoff's appointment, which the judge determined was unconstitutional. Bastian questioned the purpose of granting courts the power to fill prosecutor vacancies if the president could immediately undo such appointments. Rogoff's attorney, Hailyn Chen, argued that the Constitution's Appointments Clause was designed to prevent executive cronyism, not to grant unchecked presidential authority. item.description: George Russell, driver for Mercedes in Formula 1, has admitted that the team has been surprised by the frequency of upgrades introduced by their competitors this season. Speaking to media including GPblog, Russell explained that Mercedes has been struggling to match the pace of development from rival teams such as Red Bull and McLaren, despite the cost cap restrictions. He noted that while Mercedes has maintained strong form throughout the season, their competitors have continued to bring significant developments. He mentioned that Red Bull has already confirmed their last package introduced at Azerbaijan will be their final one for the 2026 season. item.title: Trump's Texas Campaign Event Draws Small Crowd Amid Criticism of Remarks on Veganism and Affordability
item.description: President Donald Trump's recent campaign stop in Texas was described as a 'disastrous' event by progressive commentator Ben Meiselas on 'The MeidasTouch Podcast.' item.title: Vintage Photos Capture Pre-War Hollywood Glamour on Catalina Island in 1941
item.description: In June 1941, Columbia Pictures starlets Betty Brooks and Patti McCarty spent a weekend on Santa Catalina Island off the coast of Southern California, capturing classic pre-WWII Hollywood glamour and leisure. Shot by LIFE photographer Peter Stackpole, this photo essay documented the care-free summer adventures of the two 20-year-olds. At the time, both McCarty and Brooks were aspiring contract 'bit players' who had recently signed with Columbia Pictures and quickly became close friends. LIFE framed the trip as a special 'treat' for the young starlets. Patti McCarty had never previously traveled off the California mainland, and Betty Brooks had never stepped foot on a boat before the trip. Stackpole captured them enjoying classic Catalina pastimes—riding in speedboats, looking through glass-bottom boats, posing on the rocky shore, and playing with local wildlife like a white peacock. item.description: In a recent interview with Time magazine, former President Donald Trump made statements that could have legal implications for his administration, according to Ted Boutros, CNN's attorney. Boutros, who is representing CNN in a lawsuit against the White House over restrictions on the network's reporters, expressed surprise that Trump appeared unaware of a federal judge's order regarding press access. During the interview, Trump was asked if he was ignoring an order from U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, to which he responded, 'I'm not ignoring his order. item.description: Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) confronted Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), during a congressional hearing on Thursday, accusing him of unlawfully reducing the office of the agency's inspector general. The New York Times reported that Pulte has moved to significantly shrink the inspector general's office, which polices the FHFA and oversees multitrillion-dollar mortgage markets. Warren cited a letter from inspector general staff members to Congress, stating that staffing cuts of 70-80% in fiscal year 2027 would halt nearly all criminal investigations. item.title: Nicolle Wallace Mocks Eric Schmitt's Flawed Defense After Senate Hearing Misstep
item.description: Nicolle Wallace, host of MS NOW, expressed strong criticism toward Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) following his performance during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing involving former special counsel Jack Smith. Schmitt attempted to question Smith about his presence at an Atlanta Hawks game, claiming Smith had perjured himself by denying attendance. However, it was revealed that Smith had actually been at an Iowa Hawkeyes away game in Maryland, a fact that Democrats on the committee quickly exposed. item.title: Trump's Approval Rating Hits Historic Low Amid Economic Discontent
item.description: President Donald Trump's approval rating has plummeted to an 'extremely rare' level according to recent polling data, with 82 percent of Americans disapproving of his handling of cost-of-living issues. A new AP-NORC poll released Thursday shows a staggering 82 percent disapproval rate compared to 17 percent approval, while other polls from Reuters-Ipsos, Marquette Law School, and CNN also indicate approval ratings in the high teens and disapproval rates around 80 percent. This level of consensus against the president is described as 'extremely rare' in American political history, with few issues generating such widespread disapproval in recent presidential terms. Economic challenges have historically been a significant factor in presidential unpopularity, but Trump's current disapproval ratings surpass those seen during the 2008 financial crisis under George W. item.title: South West Water Fined £7.8 Million for Hundreds of Sewage Spills in Devon and Cornwall
item.description:
South West Water has been ordered to pay a record fine of nearly £8 million following a six-year period of environmental offenses involving hundreds of sewage spills across Devon and Cornwall. The penalty, handed down at Plymouth Magistrates' Court on September 29, 2026, marks the largest fine ever imposed for environmental violations in the region.
The water utility pleaded guilty to 18 charges, including 17 counts of illegal water discharge and one count of failing to take reasonable remedial measures after a pumping station failure. The offenses occurred between January 2015 and July 2021 at locations including Bodmin, Harlyn, Playing Place, Polperro, and Plymouth.
Among the most serious incidents, untreated sewage was discharged onto Harlyn Beach, a popular tourist destination, on 231 occasions between 2016 and 2021. OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman and his wife, Anna, have withdrawn their planned second $25 million donation to Leading the Future, a super PAC that supports artificial intelligence-related political advocacy. item.title: Whole Fruit Consumption Associated with Improved Cardiovascular Health, Study of 371,000 Americans Finds
item.description: A recent study published in Current Developments in Nutrition has found that consuming whole fruit is associated with better cardiovascular health, while the benefits of 100 percent fruit juice are less clear. The research analyzed the dietary habits of 371,000 participants from the United States, examining the relationship between fruit intake and cardiovascular disease (CVD) outcomes. The study found that higher consumption of whole fruit correlated with lower rates of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, coronary heart disease, and heart attacks. In contrast, the data on fruit juice showed no consistent pattern of association with CVD conditions, with only minor statistically significant links between juice consumption and heart attacks or high cholesterol. The researchers noted that the juicing process removes dietary fiber and plant chemicals called polyphenols, which are present in whole fruit and may contribute to its cardioprotective effects. item.title: Why I'm Building More Local-First Software
item.description: The article discusses the author's growing interest in developing local-first software, which prioritizes offline functionality and user data privacy. The author explains that traditional applications often require constant internet connectivity, leading to functionality loss when users are offline. In contrast, local-first applications keep core functionality and data available on the device, only using the internet for synchronization when connectivity is available. The author provides examples of how note-taking applications could work differently with local-first architecture, where data is stored locally and synchronized later. The article also explores how local-first principles can be applied to AI applications, allowing for privacy-focused tools that don't require uploading personal data to remote servers. item.title: White House Excludes CNN from Second Presidential Trip Following Judge's Ruling on Ban
item.description: The White House has excluded CNN from the press pool for President Donald Trump's second presidential trip since a federal judge halted the administration's ban on the network. According to a report by NBC News, the White House had initially included CNN in the rotation schedule for the trip, which included stops at a truck plant in Denton, Texas, and a speech in Durant, Oklahoma. However, CNN was notably absent from the daily guidance released for the trip. This exclusion follows a federal judge's recent order that paused Trump's attempt to bar CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House grounds. The judge's ruling, however, only covered access to the White House grounds, leaving the administration room to sideline the outlets elsewhere. The Department of Justice filed a complaint with the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals against U.S. District Judges Patrick Schiltz and John Tunheim, along with unnamed colleagues on Minnesota's federal bench. It also seeks an investigation into judges who 'covet publicity.'

item.description: A former CIA officer, Marc Polymeropoulos, a 26-year veteran of the agency, has raised concerns about the current state of U.S. counterterrorism efforts under the Trump administration. Speaking during an interview with national security reporter Michael Weiss for the 'Bulwark Takes' program, Polymeropoulos highlighted the administration's reduction of counterterrorism resources and personnel, particularly in regions like Africa, where ungoverned spaces pose significant security risks. He expressed worry that the U.S. has become complacent about terrorism threats, more than two decades after the 9/11 attacks. Polymeropoulos emphasized that the U.S. government has finite resources, and diverting personnel and intelligence assets from counterterrorism missions to focus on immigration enforcement, such as border security at Home Depot, is making the country less safe. item.title: Speech Pathologist Warns McConnell's Automatic Gestures May Indicate Unhealing Brain Injury
item.description: Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) has been observed making automatic gestures such as thumbs-up and waving, which a speech-language pathologist has suggested may mask a likely brain injury caused by oxygen deprivation. Hilary Shae, a licensed speech-language pathologist specializing in concussion and neurological disorders, discussed these observations on 'The David Pakman Show,' emphasizing that she was not diagnosing McConnell but noting concerning patterns. Shae referenced McConnell's reported 'fall with pneumonia' and a 911 call indicating someone was 'down' before CPR was administered, suggesting a period of oxygen deprivation. She explained that McConnell's gestures, such as thumbs-up and hand-waving, are 'stereotypic gestures'—automatic responses often seen in cases of significant brain damage. item.description: According to a report by MS NOW, Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) was warned by Republican staff on the Senate Judiciary Committee that the texts he intended to use to accuse former special counsel Jack Smith of perjury were unvetted. item.title: Multidisciplinary Care Essential for Effective Migraine Management
item.description: Migraine is a complex neurological disorder that affects more than just the head, impacting multiple body systems and significantly disrupting daily life. According to Deirdre Ní Mhórdha of the Migraine Association of Ireland, effective management requires a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach that addresses the full spectrum of symptoms and their impact on patients' lives. The article emphasizes that migraine affects over one billion people globally, making it one of the most disabling conditions worldwide, particularly for women under 50. Despite its prevalence, migraine remains under-recognized, under-diagnosed, and under-treated. The condition presents with a wide range of symptoms beyond headache, including nausea, dizziness, cognitive difficulties, fatigue, anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances, and even temporary paralysis. item.title: AI Coding Assistants Rarely Verify Software Origins Before Installation Despite Available Security Features
item.description: A comprehensive study involving 1,920 trials across six open-source research projects, including three focused on high-performance computing and three on quantum computing, has revealed that AI coding assistants rarely verify the origins of software before installation. The research, published by Pengyin Shan, found that these assistants opened provenance signals—data confirming software origins—in only nine instances, representing a rate of just 0.5 percent compared to zero in 384 control trials without such signals. Despite the availability of security features like software bills of materials (which list components within a software artifact) and cryptographic signatures (which confirm authenticity), the assistants failed to actively utilize these trust signals during installation processes. item.title: David Pakman Dissects Trump's Misleading Convention Viewership Claim
item.description: Progressive political analyst David Pakman addressed President Donald Trump's recent claim about the viewership of the Republican midterm convention during a segment on 'The David Pakman Show.' Trump had boasted that the convention, held a few weeks prior, attracted 107 million views across all platforms, surpassing the NFL's 25 million viewers. Pakman clarified that Trump's figure combined all platforms, including online streams and clips, while the actual TV viewership was approximately three million, according to Nielsen. He emphasized that comparing the total views across platforms to traditional TV viewership was misleading, stating, 'It's not even that impressive.' Pakman further explained that the NFL drew 20-25 million television viewers, whereas the convention had about three million, making the comparison apples to apples. item.title: Eclipse Foundation Establishes Sovereign AI Foundation to Promote Open Source AI Control
item.description: The Eclipse Foundation, a leading global open source software foundation, has announced the creation of the Sovereign AI Foundation, a vendor-neutral initiative designed to help organizations navigate the complexities of AI dependencies and make more informed decisions about the technologies they rely on. This new foundation aims to connect industry needs with open source AI projects, fostering greater choice and control over critical AI systems. As AI transitions from experimental phases to essential operational and decision-making tools, organizations face challenges in understanding, adapting, and governing the AI technologies they depend on. The Sovereign AI Foundation addresses these concerns by providing a neutral forum where member organizations can share knowledge, evaluate open source alternatives, and collaborate on practical solutions. item.title: Ted Cruz blocks AI deepfake lawsuit bill, reigniting GOP rift with Marsha Blackburn
item.description: U.S. Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX) has blocked a bill that would allow people to sue over AI-generated deepfakes on the Senate floor, reigniting a long-standing dispute with fellow Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) over AI regulation. According to Politico, Blackburn attempted to fast-track her NO FAKES Act through unanimous consent, a procedure that typically requires no formal vote but allows any single senator to block it by objecting in person. Cruz objected, arguing the bill was not ready due to free speech concerns, including whether AI-generated content like images and videos shared by figures such as Donald Trump on social media, or satirical content from outlets like The Onion, could be mistakenly deemed illegal under the legislation. Blackburn defended the bill, stating it would establish clear guardrails to protect creators nationwide while creating a federal intellectual property right for every American's voice and visual likeness. item.title: Michigan Senate Candidate Avoids Questions on Church Abuse Scandal Ties
item.description: Republican Mike Rogers, a candidate for the U.S. Senate in Michigan's November 3 midterm elections, faced questions about his campaign's continued association with a pastor linked to a notorious church sex abuse case. During a press event in Saginaw, Rogers was pressed by reporters regarding his Faith Leadership Coalition, which includes two pastors connected to the Living Word Church network. item.description: A senior policy and tax adviser to House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA), Curt Beaulieu, had planned a weeklong European trip to Italy and France in late October, which included luxury stops at a Ferrari factory near Bologna, a Barilla pasta and cheese processor in Parma, and visits to luxury goods companies in Milan or Florence. The delegation was also scheduled to travel to France for excursions to the Champagne region and a meeting at the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). item.description: The Wall Street Journal's editorial board has criticized President Donald Trump for his recent attacks on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, following a watchdog report that cleared Powell of any criminal wrongdoing. item.description: The 1912 Baker Electric Model W Runabout represents a significant piece of automotive history, showcasing the early development of electric vehicles in the United States. Produced by the Baker Motor Vehicle Company of Cleveland, Ohio, this model was one of the leading electric cars during the Brass Era, a period known for its innovative but short-lived electric vehicle industry. The Model W Runabout featured a compact, stylish open body designed specifically for urban driving, offering a quiet and clean alternative to the noisy and polluting gasoline-powered vehicles of the time. Its electric motor provided a smooth and efficient driving experience, appealing to those who sought both ease of use and sophistication in their transportation. The Baker Electric was not only a technological marvel for its era but also a symbol of the early promise of electric motoring, which has seen a resurgence in modern times. item.description: With crucial midterm elections just weeks away, the White House is using taxpayer funds to air campaign-style TV ads featuring U.S. President Donald Trump. item.title: Federal Judge Rejects Trump DOJ's Request for Georgia Voter Data Under Privacy Laws
item.description: A federal judge in Georgia has dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Trump Justice Department (DOJ) seeking access to Georgia voters' Social Security numbers, driver's license information, and other private data. U.S. District Judge Victoria Marie Calvert ruled that the Civil Rights Act of 1960 does not override Georgia's state laws protecting voter privacy. The DOJ had demanded the unredacted voter registration list in July 2025, claiming it needed the data to verify citizenship status through the Department of Homeland Security's SAVE database. Georgia's Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger's office, however, provided a redacted version of the list, removing sensitive information as required by state law. The DOJ then sued under Title III of the Civil Rights Act, arguing federal law should take precedence. item.description: According to a report by Wired, published in Raw Story, President Donald Trump's aides are privately expressing concern that the Republican Party may suffer a significant defeat in the upcoming midterm elections. The aides are preparing for the possibility that Republicans lose control of both the House and Senate, a scenario that has not been widely discussed publicly. The report indicates that Trump's national poll numbers have declined sharply, with a recent Wall Street Journal poll showing his approval rating at 37 percent—the lowest for any president heading into midterms since polling began in 1990. item.description: Former House Republican leader Patrick McHenry criticized Texas Senate nominee Ken Paxton for making negative comments about President Donald Trump, whom McHenry credited with creating Paxton's political career. item.title: Blacktip Sharks Detect and Orient Away from Sounds Up to 243 Feet Away, Study Reveals
item.description: A groundbreaking study conducted by Florida Atlantic University has revealed that blacktip sharks (Carcharhinus limbatus) can detect low-frequency sounds from nearly 250 feet away and precisely determine their direction. Published in Integrative Organismal Biology, the research provides the first quantified evidence that free-swimming sharks can detect and orient away from sounds in the acoustic far field. The experiments, carried out off the Florida coast, involved playing low-frequency sounds ranging from 100 to 800 Hertz to wild sharks in their natural habitat. Researchers used underwater speakers, drones, and calibrated hydrophones to measure sound levels and track shark movements. The sharks reacted to all three low-frequency sound ranges but showed no response to a 10 kiloHertz control sound, which lies beyond their known hearing range. They detected sounds from distances of up to 74 meters (243 feet), substantially farther than previously demonstrated in freely swimming sharks.

item.title: AI Speech Analysis Tool Predicts Biological Ageing Through Vocal Characteristics
item.description: A groundbreaking study published in Science Advances has introduced an AI-powered 'speech clock' that assesses how quickly a person is ageing based on vocal characteristics. Developed by researchers at Adolfo Ibáñez University in Santiago, this innovative tool analyzes over 700 speech features including pitch, talking speed, and emotional content to estimate biological age. The research team recorded 2,928 Spanish speakers from multiple Latin American countries while they completed various speech tasks, including individuals with cognitive impairments and dementia. The AI model successfully distinguished between healthy individuals and those with cognitive issues by identifying a 'speech age gap' - the difference between predicted speech age and chronological age. Large speech age gaps were strongly associated with cognitive decline, suggesting the tool could serve as an early indicator for conditions like dementia. item.description: CNN fact-checker Daniel Dale has debunked President Donald Trump's recent claim that he is the only president to donate his salary while in office. Trump made the statement during a Wednesday appearance, asserting that he was the sole president to do so, though he acknowledged that George Washington 'maybe' did the same. Dale also corrected Trump's assertion that presidents are paid $550,000 annually, clarifying that the base salary is $400,000, with additional expense and travel allocations potentially raising the total to $550,000. Additionally, Dale addressed Trump's claim that he 'never got a story' about donating his salary during his first term, noting that such coverage was regular when Trump announced his donations. item.title: Butterfly Wing Patterns Create Motion Dazzle Effect to Confuse Predators
item.description: A recent study published in the journal Nature reveals that butterfly wing patterns and flight dynamics create a visual illusion known as 'motion dazzle,' which makes it difficult for predators to accurately gauge a butterfly's speed and direction. The research, led by scientists from the University of Exeter, demonstrates that the stripes and spots on butterfly wings interfere with predators' visual systems, creating false motion cues that disrupt the predator's ability to target and capture the butterfly. This effect is similar to the well-known barbershop pole illusion, where rotating striped poles appear to move upward rather than rotating. The study combined high-speed video analysis of butterfly flight, simulations of nearly 400 European butterfly species, and human interaction experiments with virtual butterflies. item.title: 120-Million-Year-Old Fossil Pushes Back Origin of Marsupial Lineage
item.description: A newly discovered fossil of Archetheridium sinense, a deltatheroidan mammal from China, has pushed back the origin of the marsupial lineage by approximately 10 million years. The fossil, dating to the Early Cretaceous period (120 million years ago), was found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, northeastern China. This discovery represents the earliest unambiguous metatherian, the broader group that includes marsupials and their extinct relatives, ever identified. The fossil includes a partial skull, jaws, nearly complete upper teeth, and portions of the limbs and spine, which is rare for early metatherian fossils that are typically limited to teeth or jaw fragments. Researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Dr. Hai-Bing Wang and Dr. Yuan-Qing Wang, suggest that Asia, rather than North America, may have been the center of origin for marsupial-line mammals. item.description: US allies Israel and Saudi Arabia scrambled fighter jets early Wednesday morning in response to an incident aboard a FlyDubai flight that Israeli journalist Amit Segal reported was being treated as a 'full-fledged terrorist attack.' According to Segal's social media statement, the co-pilot repeatedly stabbed the captain, prompting several crew members and passengers to break through the cockpit door and subdue the attacker. The incident occurred on FlyDubai Flight FZ1073, which was en route to Israel but was diverted to Saudi Arabia after the attack. The Boeing 737 aircraft experienced a sudden and rapid descent of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before transmitting an emergency signal, as reported by Flightradar24. Israel scrambled fighter jets in response to the incident, though they turned back before entering Saudi Arabian airspace, while Saudi Arabia scrambled jets to investigate, according to The New York Times citing an unnamed Israeli official. item.title: Vintage Everyday Features 20 Black and White Photos from the 1958 Brussels World's Fair
item.description: Vintage Everyday has published a collection of 20 black and white photographs capturing the 1958 Brussels World's Fair, also known as Expo 58. The images, sourced from Alex Clymans, showcase the event's iconic architecture, including the Atomium, which became the symbol of the fair. The photographs depict various international pavilions, such as the American and Soviet Union pavilions, as well as the Congolese Gardens and the Philips Pavilion designed by Le Corbusier. The collection also includes images of the cable cars, the Grand Palais, and crowds of visitors enjoying the postwar era's optimistic atmosphere. The fair, held in the aftermath of World War II, represented a period of reconstruction and international cooperation, with the Atomium standing as a testament to the era's technological and architectural innovation. These photographs provide a vivid visual record of one of the most memorable world's fairs of the 20th century, preserving the modernist structures and the vibrant

item.title: Trump and Tech Leaders Agree on Self-Regulation Framework for AI Development Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: President Donald Trump has rejected the notion of new government regulations for artificial intelligence, stating that existing laws and industry self-regulation are sufficient to address potential risks. Following a White House meeting with top technology executives, including Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and SpaceX's Elon Musk, Trump announced an agreement where tech companies will partner with external auditors to conduct safety assessments of AI models and implement stronger internal controls. The president emphasized that companies are 'self-policing' and that the Department of Justice and FBI already provide regulatory oversight. During the meeting, Trump also floated the idea of forming a committee of about 10 people to oversee AI development, though he provided no further details. Industry leaders largely supported Trump's hands-off approach, with Huang stating there is 'no conflict between innovation, technology, and safety.' The agreement comes amid growing

item.title: Mozilla Unveils Redesigned Firefox for Desktop and Mobile with Compact Mode and Theme Picker
item.description: Mozilla has rolled out a significant redesign of its Firefox browser across both desktop and mobile platforms, marking a notable update for users. The new version reintroduces compact mode, a feature previously removed by Mozilla, which minimizes the space taken by toolbars and tabs, allowing users to view more of the website content. Additionally, the redesign includes a theme picker with wallpaper options and the ability to organize shortcuts on the New Tab page. Privacy settings have been made easier to locate, and Mozilla claims the update does not compromise performance. The browser's themes, icons, and colors have been modernized to align with recent additions, such as a single off switch for generative AI tools. While features like tab groups, split view, and vertical tabs are not prominently displayed, they remain accessible for users who prefer them. Mozilla emphasized that the redesign prioritizes accessibility, ensuring customization options are inclusive for all users. The

item.title: The Historic Photograph of Victor Hugo on His Deathbed Captured by Nadar in 1885
item.description: Victor Hugo, the legendary French poet, playwright, and novelist, passed away from pneumonia on May 22, 1885, at the age of 83. By the time of his death, Hugo was a revered national hero who had dominated French literature and politics for over half a century. The day after his passing—May 23, 1885—his close circle called upon his longtime friend, the famous pioneer photographer Gaspard-Félix Tournachon, better known as Nadar. Nadar rushed to Hugo's home on Avenue Victor Hugo in Paris to immortalize the great man one last time. Taking the photograph required careful staging to accommodate the early camera technology and the solemnity of the room. Nadar refused to carry heavy artificial lighting equipment. Instead, his friend Paul Meurice helped him secure permission to throw open the window shutters overlooking the garden. To control the harsh morning sun, Nadar rigged black drapery across the window and tied it to a bedpost. This isolated Hugo's face against a dark, somber background.

item.title: Nest Egg: A Wooden Egg Toy That Helps Children Learn Financial Responsibility
item.description: The Nest Egg is a unique financial education tool designed for children, featuring a wooden egg-shaped toy that serves as a physical representation of saving money. Unlike traditional digital solutions, Nest Egg focuses on tactile learning, allowing children to physically interact with the concept of saving through a tangible object. The product, developed by Senser Woodcraft, combines traditional craftsmanship with modern financial education principles. The wooden egg, which can be filled with coins or small items, is designed to help children understand the concept of saving in a way that feels natural and intuitive. The product's design philosophy emphasizes that children may grasp financial concepts more effectively when they can hold and interact with a physical object rather than relying solely on digital interfaces. This approach aligns with educational theories that suggest hands-on learning can be more effective for young children than screen-based learning. The Nest Egg is pa

item.title: Influencers Face Backlash for Inappropriate Behavior at Historical Sites
item.description: The Ingham Family has recently faced significant backlash for posting inappropriate photos at Auschwitz, a site of immense historical significance. The family's actions have sparked outrage among the public and historical preservation groups, who emphasize the importance of respecting such sites. The incident highlights a growing trend of influencers and tourists engaging in disrespectful behavior at historical and memorial locations, including taking selfies, making jokes, and even engaging in what has been termed 'sushi terrorism'—a term used to describe the act of eating sushi in inappropriate places like museums or historical sites. This behavior not only disrespects the memory of those who suffered but also undermines the educational value of these sites. The Daily Mail Online has reported on several similar incidents, where influencers have faced criticism for their actions. The article calls for greater awareness and respect for historical sites, urging travelers to consider the

item.title: Ukrainian Polls Show Declining Support for Zelensky Amid Corruption Concerns
item.description: According to recent polling data, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's favorability ratings have significantly declined, with only 28 percent of Ukrainians expressing a desire for him to remain president after the war. A fifth of those who distrust him cite corruption as the main reason, and 59 percent of Ukrainians blame Zelensky personally for the extent of corruption in Ukraine. The article highlights that if elections were held today, Zelensky would likely struggle to finish in the top three, with polls indicating he would lose to potential rivals such as former Commander-in-Chief Valeriy Zaluzhny, former intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov, and even former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The article also addresses constitutional concerns, noting that while Ukrainian law prohibits elections during martial law, the constitution (Article 83) does not extend the president's term, a deliberate omission to prevent future presidents from declaring martial law to avoid removal from o

item.title: NASA Extends Boeing Starliner Contracts Amid Crew Dragon Retirement Plans
item.description: NASA has announced its decision to exercise options for two additional flights on Boeing's Starliner spacecraft, while also providing financial support to help the company return the vehicle to service and find a new rocket after the Atlas V's retirement. This move confirms earlier reporting by Ars Technica about NASA's plans to maintain access to low-Earth orbit following the impending retirement of SpaceX's Crew Dragon vehicle. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman noted that SpaceX intends to phase out older platforms like Falcon and Dragon in favor of their next-generation Starship system. Boeing's Starliner has faced significant challenges, including thruster issues during its first crewed test flight in June 2024 that nearly led to a catastrophic loss of astronauts. The company has incurred over $2 billion in losses for the Starliner program, with NASA having already provided $5.1 billion under the Commercial Crew program. NASA will pay Boeing $359 million to complete a rebuild of th

item.title: Apple Pay Begins Rollout in India with Axis Bank Partnership Amid UPI Dominance
item.description: Apple Pay has officially launched in India, marking a significant milestone after years of delays in the world's most populous country. The service, initially rolled out on Tuesday, partners with Axis Bank, India's third-largest private-sector lender, to enable Apple Pay functionality for eligible Visa and Mastercard users. This launch comes after years of anticipation, as Apple had been preparing to enter the Indian market, which is dominated by the state-backed Unified Payments Interface (UPI) system. UPI has become the backbone of India's digital payments ecosystem, allowing instant bank-to-bank transactions without the need for physical cards. In contrast, Apple Pay is card-based and requires integration with individual banks and payment infrastructure providers, making a broader rollout more complex. The initial launch is limited to Axis Bank cards, with acceptance restricted to merchants and terminals that have been enabled for the service. Apple is seeking a transaction fee of a

item.title: 30 portadas vintage de la revista Flying Aces de los años 30
item.description: La revista Flying Aces, publicada por primera vez en 1928 por Periodical House, se convirtió en una de las revistas pulp más populares y influyentes dedicadas a la aventura aérea durante la Edad de Oro de la Aviación. Durante su apogeo, la revista cautivó a los lectores con relatos emocionantes de pilotos valientes, combate aéreo y hazañas heroicas ambientadas en la Primera Guerra Mundial y el período interbelico. La revista combinaba ficción de ritmo rápido con artículos sobre aviones reales, ilustraciones técnicas y arte de portada colorido que capturaba la romance y el peligro del vuelo temprano. Entre sus colaboradores destacaron escritores como Arch Whitehouse, George Bruce y Frederick C. Painton. A su máximo esplendor, Flying Aces inspiró a generaciones de jóvenes lectores a soñar con convertirse en pilotos y jugó un papel significativo en popularizar la cultura aeronáutica en Estados Unidos durante la década de 1930 y principios de la de 1940. Estas 30 portadas vintage de la rev

item.title: Christa Vogel: Icono de la alta costura de la era dorada
item.description: Christa Vogel fue una modelo de moda alemana que se convirtió en una de las caras más elegantes y reconocibles en la fotografía de moda internacional durante finales de los años 50 y principios de los 60. Conocida por su belleza refinada, su porte grácil y sus rasgos sofisticados, Vogel apareció en numerosos reportajes editoriales de alto nivel para revistas como Life, Vogue y Harper's Bazaar. Fotografiada por legendarios fotógrafos como Horst P. Horst, F.C. Gundlach, Karen Radkai y Mark Shaw, representó el estilo chic y ladylike de la época, modelando habitualmente haute couture de diseñadores como Dior, Balenciaga y otras casas de moda líderes. Sus imágenes atemporales siguen siendo apreciadas hoy en día por coleccionistas de fotografía de moda vintage, representando el apogeo de la elegancia europea posguerra y los estándares clásicos de modelaje. La noticia presenta una serie de fotografías de Vogel en diferentes looks de los años 50 y 60, destacando prendas de diseñadores como Gre

item.title: A la izquierda del PSOE: no nos abochornen más
item.description: El artículo analiza la falta de claridad y acción política por parte del PSOE y la izquierda en España frente a la crisis de vivienda, un problema crítico para la mayoría de ciudadanos. El PSOE, liderado por Pedro Sánchez, ha sido incapaz de presentar medidas efectivas o una posición clara sobre la vivienda como derecho, con la única respuesta notable siendo la de José Luis Ábalos en 2021, quien declaró que 'la vivienda es un derecho, pero también un bien de mercado'. La izquierda, incluyendo a Podemos, Izquierda Unida y partidos del espacio Sumar, tiene un discurso claro sobre la vivienda como derecho básico, pero carece de liderazgos definidos y estrategias electorales claras a menos de siete semanas de las elecciones. El artículo critica la falta de cohesión y la autopostulación de líderes en la izquierda madrileña, señalando que el verdadero movimiento político está en las calles, representado por los acampados, manifestantes y sindicatos de inquilinas y estudiantes. Estos grupos h

item.title: PP y Vox podrían alcanzar mayoría absoluta en elecciones generales de 2026
item.description: Según el promedio de encuestas de DatosRTVE publicado el 6 de octubre de 2026, el Partido Popular (PP) obtendría 137 escaños en las elecciones generales convocadas para el 29 de noviembre de 2026, lo que le permitiría gobernar en coalición con Vox. El PP necesitaría los 65 escaños de Vox para alcanzar la mayoría absoluta, superando los 200 diputados necesarios para investir a un presidente. El PSOE, en tanto, perdería 17 escaños respecto a 2023, descendiendo de 121 a 104 escaños, y su bloque de investidura quedaría en 145 escaños, insuficiente para reeditar el pacto de 2023. Sumar, que formó parte del gobierno de coalición, se hundiría de 31 a 10 escaños, mientras que Vox aumentaría de 33 a 65 escaños, consolidándose como tercera fuerza. En términos de porcentaje de voto, el PP ganaría con un 32,5%, el PSOE caería a 26,3%, Vox subiría a 18,7% y Sumar se reduciría a un 6,3%. El análisis señala que el CIS, una encuestadora con una muestra amplia de 4.000 personas, distorsiona ligeramente

item.title: Boda de Anna Nicole Smith y J. Howard Marshall II: Un evento mediático de los años 90 con un diferencial de edad de 63 años
item.description: El 27 de junio de 1994, la modelo y actriz Anna Nicole Smith, de 26 años, se casó con el multimillonario petrolero J. Howard Marshall II, de 89 años, en la White Dove Wedding Chapel de Houston, Texas. La ceremonia, celebrada con solo once invitados, se convirtió en un evento mediático emblemático de los años 90 debido a la diferencia de edad de 63 años y la fortuna millonaria de Marshall. Smith, que trabajaba como bailarina en un club de Houston antes de alcanzar fama como Playmate de Playboy y modelo de Guess, conoció a Marshall en 1991 en un club de striptease. Marshall, atraído por ella, le propuso matrimonio varias veces y le regaló millones en propiedades, automóviles de lujo y joyas. La unión generó críticas y acusaciones de que Smith era una 'buscadora de oro' interesada en la fortuna de Marshall, estimada en 1.600 millones de dólares. Smith siempre afirmó amar genuinamente a Marshall, quien le brindó estabilidad a ella y a su hijo. Tras la boda, Smith abandonó a Marshall para i

item.title: 35 retratos glamurosos de Janet Gaynor en los años 20 del siglo XX
item.description: La noticia presenta una colección de 35 retratos de Janet Gaynor, actriz estadounidense de la época de los años 20 del siglo XX. Janet Gaynor, nacida como Laura Augusta Gainor el 6 de octubre de 1906 y fallecida el 14 de septiembre de 1984, comenzó su carrera en el cine como extra en cortometrajes y películas a finales de 1924 en los estudios Hal Roach. Adoptó el nombre artístico Janet Gaynor a sugerencia de su padrastro. En 1926, logró un papel secundario como Anna Burger en la película 'The Johnstown Flood' de Fox, lo que le valió un contrato de cinco años con Fox Film Corporation. Ese mismo año fue nombrada WAMPAS Baby Star junto a otras actrices como Joan Crawford, Dolores del Río y Mary Astor, y apareció en otras películas de Fox como 'The Shamrock Handicap', 'The Midnight Kiss', 'The Blue Eagle' y 'The Return of Peter Grimm'. Para 1927, Gaynor se había consolidado como actriz principal en Fox, conocida por su imagen dulce, pura y vulnerable en pantalla, a menudo comparada con la

item.title: El decreto de vivienda amplía hasta 2030 la prohibición de compras especulativas por parte de fondos buitre
item.description: El Gobierno español ha aprobado un decreto que prolonga hasta el año 2030 la prohibición de que los fondos buitre adquieran viviendas en el mercado secundario con fines especulativos. Esta medida, que se enmarca dentro de las políticas de vivienda social y de lucha contra la especulación inmobiliaria, busca garantizar el acceso a la vivienda para las personas de menores ingresos y evitar que los fondos buitre, conocidos por su práctica de comprar propiedades a bajo precio para revenderlas a un precio mucho mayor, continúen generando presión en el mercado. El decreto, que se suma a otras iniciativas gubernamentales en materia de vivienda, establece que los fondos buitre no podrán adquirir más de un 20% de las viviendas en el mercado secundario en cualquier región del país. Además, se han introducido nuevas medidas para facilitar el acceso a la vivienda pública, como la creación de un fondo especial para la construcción de viviendas sociales y la simplificación de trámites para la obtenc

item.title: Marilyn Monroe reconocida por TIME Magazine como 'Icono de la Era' en homenaje a su legado en 1954
item.description: Marilyn Monroe fue seleccionada por TIME Magazine como una de sus '100 Mujeres del Año' para representar el año 1954, consolidando su legado como 'Icono de la Era'. Este proyecto retrospectivo rediseña portadas históricas de TIME para reconocer a mujeres influyentes que a menudo fueron ignoradas para el título tradicional 'Hombre del Año' durante el siglo XX. Aunque Monroe no apareció en la portada de TIME en 1954, su historia en solitario no se publicó hasta el 14 de mayo de 1956. El año 1954 fue un punto de inflexión crucial para su carrera, ya que, tras el éxito masivo de 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes' y 'How to Marry a Millionaire' a finales de 1953, entró en 1954 como la estrella más importante de Hollywood. A finales de 1954, filmó la icónica escena del graderío del metro en 'The Seven Year Itch', donde su vestido blanco ondeante se convirtió en uno de los momentos visuales más famosos de la historia del cine. El perfil de TIME honra a Monroe no solo como una genio cómico y símbolo s

item.title: Podemos y Frente Amplio avanzan en negociaciones para formar coalición electoral con primarias abiertas
item.description: La formación política Podemos ha anunciado su disposición a pactar una lista única con el Frente Amplio para las próximas elecciones, aunque con la condición de que dicha coalición sea ratificada en primarias abiertas. Según informa elDiario.es, la propuesta de Podemos incluye la celebración de primarias el 14 y 15 de octubre para validar la unión de ambas fuerzas políticas. Este anuncio se produce en un contexto de tensión interna, ya que organizaciones como Compromís han expresado su deseo de mantener una relación electoral con el Frente Amplio sin profundizar en lazos orgánicos más estrechos. Compromís, por ejemplo, busca unir en una sola lista conjunta a formaciones como Podemos, IU o Movimiento Sumar, pero sin someterse a una dirección unificada del Frente Amplio. Para Compromís, su proyecto debe ser independiente del estatal aunque mantenga coordinación con él, y conservar plena capacidad para tomar decisiones. El Frente Amplio, por su parte, ha mostrado cierta reticencia a profu

item.title: Investigadores del CSIC desarrollan un método escalable para producir electricidad a partir de calor residual
item.description: Los investigadores del Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC) han logrado desarrollar un método escalable para convertir el calor residual en electricidad de manera eficiente. Este avance tecnológico representa un paso significativo en la búsqueda de soluciones para aprovechar el exceso de calor que se genera en procesos industriales, como la fabricación de acero, la producción de cemento o la generación de energía térmica. El método, basado en materiales termoeléctricos avanzados, permite capturar el calor residual que normalmente se pierde en el ambiente y transformarlo en energía eléctrica utilizable. La escalabilidad del proceso es clave, ya que permite su implementación en una amplia gama de industrias sin requerir inversiones excesivas. Además, el método es sostenible y contribuye a reducir la huella de carbono de las empresas industriales. Este descubrimiento podría tener un impacto significativo en la transición energética global, al permitir una mayor eficienci

item.title: Fotografías inéditas del rodaje de 'Ciudadano Kane' revelan innovaciones técnicas en cine
item.description: La noticia presenta 38 fotografías inéditas del rodaje de 'Ciudadano Kane' (1941), considerada una de las películas más importantes de la historia del cine. El artículo detalla las innovaciones técnicas empleadas por Orson Welles y su equipo, destacando cómo se rompieron las normas establecidas en el cine de la época. El director, a los 25 años, utilizó su falta de experiencia para desafiar convenciones, especialmente en la construcción de sets con techos hechos de tela tensa para permitir ángulos bajos que daban una sensación de imponencia a los personajes. El equipo tuvo que perforar el suelo de los estudios para colocar cámaras por debajo del nivel del suelo, logrando ángulos visuales icónicos. La técnica de enfoque profundo, donde todo el plano permanece nítido desde primer plano hasta el fondo, fue un hito logrado mediante lentes recubiertos, iluminación intensa y compositores ópticos en cámara. item.title: El Studebaker Avanti R2 de 1963: Un diseño innovador y atrevido en la historia automovilística
item.description: La revista Vintage Everyday publicó una noticia sobre el Studebaker Avanti R2 de 1963, destacando su importancia como un vehículo emblemático de la década de 1960. Diseñado por el equipo de Raymond Loewy, este automóvil se destacó por su cuerpo de fibra de vidrio aerodinámico, parabrisas inclinado y estilo futurista que parecía adelantarse a su época. El Avanti R2 estaba equipado con un motor V8 supercargado de 289 pulgadas cúbicas que generaba 335 caballos de potencia, lo que le permitía alcanzar los 0-60 mph en menos de 7 segundos, una cifra impresionante para un automóvil de turismo de lujo en su época. Además de su rendimiento, el vehículo incorporaba características avanzadas para la época, como frenos de disco delanteros y un cockpit inspirado en aviones, combinando estilo y velocidad de manera innovadora. La publicación incluye fotografías que resaltan la elegancia atemporal y el carácter audaz del Avanti R2, presentándolo como un ejemplo de diseño automovilístico que sigue sien

item.title: Brenda Marshall: La actriz elegante de Hollywood en los años 40
item.description: Brenda Marshall (1915-1992) fue una actriz estadounidense conocida por su elegancia y actuaciones en el cine de los años 40. Nacida Ardis Ankerson en Filipinas en una familia noruegodescendiente, Marshall ganó fama con papeles memorables en películas de aventuras clásicas como 'The Sea Hawk' (1940) junto a Errol Flynn y 'Captains of the Clouds' (1942). Con su cabello oscuro, rasgos refinados y presencia en pantalla sofisticada, interpretó a mujeres fuertes y glamorosas en películas de aventuras y dramas. Estuvo casada con el actor William Holden desde 1941 hasta 1971, una de las uniones más destacadas de Hollywood en su época. Aunque su carrera actoral fue relativamente breve, Marshall dejó una impresión duradera como una de las estrellas más graciosas y subestimadas de la Era de Oro del cine. Estas fotos vintage capturan perfectamente el encanto perdurable y el atractivo sofisticado de Brenda Marshall. La noticia, publicada en Vintage Everyday el 11 de julio de 2026, destaca su legado

item.title: PP y Vox rechazan limitar los alquileres en Baleares a pesar de las protestas ciudadanas
item.description: La noticia aborda la postura del Govern de las Islas Baleares, liderado por el Partido Popular (PP), y la oposición de Vox en relación con la regulación de los alquileres y la vivienda. Según el texto, en marzo de 2025, ambos partidos impidieron que prosperara una proposición de ley del PSIB-PSOE destinada a declarar zonas tensionadas y limitar los alquileres. En diciembre de 2025, cuando se planteó la renovación de miles de contratos de alquiler, el Ejecutivo optó por preparar incentivos fiscales para los propietarios en lugar de declarar Balears zona tensionada. Asimismo, en febrero de 2026, PP y Vox rechazaron limitar temporalmente la adquisición de vivienda por no residentes y grandes tenedores en municipios tensionados, así como elevar la fiscalidad sobre las operaciones inmobiliarias de lujo y las compras de multipropietarios. item.title: La Audiencia Provincial rechaza la intervención de móviles en caso de filtración de atestado policial por desproporción y afectación al secreto de las comunicaciones
item.description: La Audiencia Provincial de Madrid ha rechazado el recurso presentado por las acusaciones en el procedimiento judicial contra la alcaldesa de Alcalá de Henares, Judith Piquet, por supuestamente filtrar un atestado policial. Las acusaciones habían solicitado la intervención de los móviles de la alcaldesa, del entonces jefe de la Policía Local, del director de comunicación del ayuntamiento y del concejal de seguridad. Sin embargo, los magistrados han considerado que dicha medida sería desproporcionada y no útil para la investigación, ya que afecta directamente al derecho constitucional al secreto de las comunicaciones y a la intimidad de las personas. La resolución señala que la intervención de dispositivos móviles no es proporcional a los hechos investigados, que consisten en una presunta infidelidad en la custodia de un documento. Además, los magistrados han destacado que el denunciante principal, el exjefe de la Policía Local, fue supuestamente uno de los intervinientes en revelar secr

item.title: Detrás de cámaras: Imágenes inéditas de la sesión fotográfica de Vogue con personajes de Star Wars en 1977
item.description:
La revista Vogue publicó en noviembre de 1977 una edición especial que combinó el mundo del cine y la moda de manera inusual, presentando una sesión fotográfica que integraba personajes de Star Wars con supermodelos. La sesión, titulada 'The Force of Fur', fue realizada por el fotógrafo Eisuke Ishimuro y estilizada por Jade Hobson. El proyecto surgió poco después del éxito mundial de Star Wars, cuando George Lucas autorizó a personajes como Darth Vader, C-3PO, Stormtroopers, Jawas y Snaggletooth a posar junto a la modelo Jerry Hall y Maria Hanson para mostrar las piezas de piel y joyería de la temporada de invierno.
Ishimuro optó por un enfoque visual diferente al tradicional, utilizando iluminación plana y directa para lograr un efecto bidimensional, casi como un cómic, en contraste con la complejidad de los efectos visuales de la película.
